verses.1: And it happened that when Jehovah raised Elia up in the sky during the storm, Elia and Elijah went out from the abyss.
verses.2: And Elijah said to Elisha, “Come here, for the LORD has sent me to Bethel.” Elisha replied, “May the LORD live and may your soul be spared if I leave you.” Then they went down to Bethel.
verses.3: And the sons of the prophets who were in Bethel went to Elijah and said to him, “You know that today Jehovah will take away your God from you.” He replied, “I also know this.”
verses.4: And Eliehu Elisha said to him, “Please stay here. May the LORD send Rehoboam to you.” Then he said, “May the LORD and your soul be with you. If I leave you, then Rehoboam will come.”
verses.5: And the sons of the prophets who were in Gibeah came to Elijah and said to him, “You know that today Jehovah will take away your throne from you.” And he said, “I also know that.”
verses.6: And Eliyah said to him, “Please stay here. For Jehovah has sent me down to this place.” Then he said, “May Jehovah live and may your soul be blessed! If I leave you, then go ahead.” And they both went away.
verses.7: And fifty men from the prophets went and stood opposite each other. They stood on the hilltops.
verses.8: And Elia took his staff, struck it against the water, and the water split into two parts. Then both of them crossed over into the other side.
verses.9: And after they had passed by, Eliezer said to Elisha, “What should I do before I go away from you?” Elisha replied, “Please have two birds in your wings.”
verses.10: And he said, “Be careful when you ask me to leave you. If I am taken away from you, it will be good for you. But if not, then it won’t be good for you.”
verses.11: And there were many who walked along, talking. Then, a flame of fire appeared, along with horses of fire. They separated from each other, and Eliyahu was carried up into the sky by the storm.
verses.12: Elisha saw him, and he cried out, “Father! Father!” But he still couldn’t see him. Then Elisha strengthened his faith and tore his clothes in two pieces.
verses.13: And he threw Aderet Eliyahu down from above. Then he sat back down and stood on the edge of the cliff.
verses.14: And he took Adonai’s rod that had fallen from him. He splashed the water with it, and said, “Where is the LORD, God of Adonai?” Then he splashed the water again, and it divided the waters. And Elisha passed over.
verses.15: And the sons of the prophets saw him in Gibeah, and they said, “May the spirit of Elijah rest upon Elisha.” Then they came to call upon him. They bowed down before him.
verses.16: And they said to him, “Please, let there be fifty men from your servants who can go and ask for your master. Then we will bring his soul back.” But he said, “Do not send them.”
verses.17: And they searched for him until evening. Then they said, “Send fifty men.” They sent fifty men, but after three days, they still couldn’t find him.
verses.18: And they returned to him. He sat in Jericho. He said to them, “I told you not to go away.”
verses.19: And the people of the city said to Elisha, “Please appoint someone who is good enough to rule over the city. For Adoni sees that the waters are bad, and the land is in a state of chaos.”
verses.20: And he said, “Take me a new egg, and put salt on it.” They did as he said.
verses.21: And he went to the place where the water was. There, he poured salt into it. He said, “As the Lord has said, ‘The healing of this water will prevent death and destruction from coming from there again.’”
verses.22: And the waters have been dried up until today, as Elijah said.
verses.23: And from there, Beth El was taken away. He went up the road, and little boys came out of the city and helped him. They said to him, “Climb up, climb up!”
verses.24: And he turned around, became angry, and cursed them in the name of Jehovah. Then two rivers rushed out from the forest, and forty-two children were drowned in those rivers.
verses.25: And he went from there to Mount Carmel. From there, he returned to Shomron.
